title.en: Anger management, word forms, and jumbled sentences

text.en: Quarrels over petty things are funny on stage, but harmful in real life. Unit 9 of Words and Expressions 2 pairs texts on anger and J. Krishnamurti's 'On Violence' with word forms, reported speech, and jumbled sentences.

Unit 9 reflects on Chekhov's one-act farce 'The Proposal', where neighbours quarrel over land and dogs instead of focusing on what matters.
Text I teaches anger management: pausing, taking five deep breaths, counting to ten, drinking water, and choosing an assertive rather than aggressive response.
Text II, J. Krishnamurti's 'On Violence', argues that true education should help us outgrow cruelty and build a sane, rational society rather than merely passing exams.
Vocabulary practises converting verbs into nouns and adverbs (e.g., encourage -> encouragement -> encouragingly; excite -> excitement -> excitedly; beautify -> beauty -> beautifully).
Grammar reinforces Reported Speech using varied reporting verbs (complain, say, inquire, mention) in a clinic dialogue.
Editing practises unscrambling jumbled sentence parts into meaningful quotes, and Listening features Chekhov's moving story 'Vanka'.
Unit 9 connects the comical quarrels of 'The Proposal' with real-life anger management and peace.
When angry, pause before responding: take deep breaths, count to ten, or drink water.
J. Krishnamurti warns that education must help us overcome violence, not just pass exams.
In Vocabulary, one root word can form a verb, noun, and adverb: 'encourage', 'encouragement', 'encouragingly'.
In clinic dialogues, choose accurate reporting verbs: 'Ashish complained that he felt sleepy all the time.'
In Chekhov's 'Vanka', a lonely nine-year-old orphan writes a heartfelt letter to his grandfather.

problem.en: Write the noun and adverb forms of the verb 'excite'.

why.en: Many verbs form abstract nouns with '-ment'.
The adverb describes doing something with excitement.

prompt.en: Explain how to manage anger constructively and how one verb can form both a noun and an adverb.

requiredIdeas.en: Pause, breathe deeply, and respond assertively rather than aggressively
Verbs can be converted to nouns (-ment/-ness) and adverbs (-ly)
Reported speech uses specific reporting verbs like complain or inquire

points.en: Anger management helps us respond calmly and constructively instead of aggressively.
J. Krishnamurti emphasises education for a sane, non-violent world.
Verbs like encourage, excite, and beautify have related noun and adverb forms.
Reported speech and jumbled-sentence editing build precision in grammar.
